title: Radiographic Protocol to Quantify Cranial Tibial Translation in Dogs
author: Adolfo Maria Tambella
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bc48iyzw

steps.title: Position the dog and limb
steps.instruction: Place the dog under general anaesthesia in lateral recumbence with the hind limb on a custom-designed radiolucent device (maintaining a 135˚ joint angle).

substeps.instruction: Allocate the femur on the immobile platform.
Secure the tibia to the mobile platform using polystyrene blocks in the respective housings.
Apply a manual force in the caudal direction to establish a zero point for translation measurement.

steps.title: Take baseline radiographic projection
steps.instruction: Take a mediolateral radiographic projection of the stifle to be evaluated, ensuring the central radiographic beam is consistently centered on each stifle.

steps.title: Apply force and take second projection
steps.instruction: Apply a standard force of 49 N to the mobile tibial platform in the horizontal plane and cranial direction, using a digital dynamometer for measurement.

substeps.instruction: Maintain the force application during the execution of the radiograph.
Take a mediolateral radiographic projection of the stifle while the force is being applied.

steps.title: Measure absolute cranial tibial translation
steps.instruction: Calculate the absolute tibial translation (ΔS) in mm using the two radiographic images.

substeps.instruction: On each image, draw two vertical, parallel lines perpendicular to the vector force and tangent to the apex of the tibial crest and the caudal edge of the femoral condyles, respectively.
Measure the distance between these two lines on the image before force application (D1).
Measure the distance between these two lines on the image during force application (D2).
Calculate absolute translation using the formula: ΔS = D2 - D1.

steps.title: Normalize tibial translation
steps.instruction: Calculate the normalized tibial translation (ΔN) to account for tibial width.

substeps.instruction: Measure the tibial width (TW) in mm in a mediolateral projection on the distal portion of the tibial crest, perpendicular to the long axis of the tibia.
Calculate normalized translation using the formula: ΔN = ΔS / TW × 100.

description: BACKGROUND Canine cranial cruciate ligament (CrCL), in addition to other biomechanical functions, prevents cranial tibial translation [1-4]. The detection of tibial translation can aid revealing stifle joint instability as a result of CrCL injury. However, clinical diagnosis of CrCL insufficiency is subjective and difficult to quantify accurately [5,6]. In order to thoroughly assess the joint stability as well as joint stabilization after surgery, it is imperative to quantify and compare joint stability between and within subjects over time. Several studies described radiographic techniques to assess translational stifle stability and CrCL integrity [6-12], but they may have some limitations: tricky execution; need for complex devices; absence of validation; failure to include a specific angle or a controlled force; tested only on experimental lesion or only ex vivo; poor applicability in vivo. This protocol aims to assess the integrity of CrCL and objectively quantifying the in vivo cranial canine stifle translation using a simple, radiolucent translator device keeping fixed the joint angle during the thrust. This protocol was validated in the following article: Tambella AM, Omini L, Attili AR, Vullo C, Martin S (2020) Evaluation of cranial tibial translation in dogs: Diagnostic accuracy of radiographic method using a simple device. PLoS ONE 15(2): e0228621. (ISSN: 1932-6203) (DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0228621) https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0228621
